title: Bear and Finding Criminals
statementMd:
There are $*n*$ cities in Bearland, numbered $1$ through $*n*$. Cities are arranged in one long row. The distance between cities $*i*$ and $*j*$ is equal to $|*i* - *j*|$.

Limak is a police officer. He lives in a city $*a*$. His job is to catch criminals. It's hard because he doesn't know in which cities criminals are. Though, he knows that there is **at most one** criminal in each city.

Limak is going to use a BCD (Bear Criminal Detector). The BCD will tell Limak how many criminals there are for every distance from a city $*a*$. After that, Limak can catch a criminal in each city for which he **is sure** that there must be a criminal.

You know in which cities criminals are. Count the number of criminals Limak will catch, after he uses the BCD.

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*a*$ ($1 ≤ *a* ≤ *n* ≤ 100$) — the number of cities and the index of city where Limak lives.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*t*_{1}, *t*_{2}, ..., *t*_{*n*}$ ($0 ≤ *t*_{*i*} ≤ 1$). There are $*t*_{*i*}$ criminals in the $*i*$-th city.

## Output

Print the number of criminals Limak will catch.

## Note

In the first sample, there are six cities and Limak lives in the third one (blue arrow below). Criminals are in cities marked red.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/74445df6818d0a935b3cc471d18d64101be6f281.png)

Using the BCD gives Limak the following information:

- There is one criminal at distance $0$ from the third city — Limak is sure that this criminal is exactly in the third city.
- There is one criminal at distance $1$ from the third city — Limak doesn't know if a criminal is in the second or fourth city.
- There are two criminals at distance $2$ from the third city — Limak is sure that there is one criminal in the first city and one in the fifth city.
- There are zero criminals for every greater distance.

So, Limak will catch criminals in cities $1$, $3$ and $5$, that is $3$ criminals in total.

In the second sample (drawing below), the BCD gives Limak the information that there is one criminal at distance $2$ from Limak's city. There is only one city at distance $2$ so Limak is sure where a criminal is.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c2bacc2aceaabacc98cc0dba179bc344f02aae9f.png)
statementZhMd:
有 $*n*$ 座城市，编号从 $1$ 到 $*n*$，位于 Bearland。所有城市排成一行。城市 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$ 之间的距离等于 $|*i* - *j*|$。

Limak 是一名警察。他住在城市 $*a*$。他的工作是抓捕罪犯。但这很困难，因为他不知道罪犯在哪些城市。不过，他知道每座城市中**至多有一名**罪犯。

Limak 打算使用 BCD（Bear Criminal Detector，熊牌罪犯探测器）。对于每个从城市 $*a*$ 出发的距离，BCD 会告诉 Limak 该距离处有多少名罪犯。之后，对于那些他**确定**一定有罪犯的城市，Limak 可以抓捕其中的罪犯。

你知道罪犯所在的城市。请计算 Limak 使用 BCD 后能够抓捕的罪犯数量。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*a*$（$1 ≤ *a* ≤ *n* ≤ 100$）——城市的数量，以及 Limak 居住的城市编号。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*t*_{1}, *t*_{2}, ..., *t*_{*n*}$（$0 ≤ *t*_{*i*} ≤ 1$）。其中 $*t*_{*i*}$ 表示第 $*i*$ 座城市中的罪犯数量。

## 输出格式

输出 Limak 能够抓捕的罪犯数量。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，共有六座城市，Limak 住在第三座城市（下图中的蓝色箭头处）。罪犯所在的城市标记为红色。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/74445df6818d0a935b3cc471d18d64101be6f281.png)

使用 BCD 后，Limak 得到以下信息：

- 距离第三座城市为 $0$ 的位置有一名罪犯——Limak 确信这名罪犯就在第三座城市。
- 距离第三座城市为 $1$ 的位置有一名罪犯——Limak 不知道罪犯是在第二座城市还是第四座城市。
- 距离第三座城市为 $2$ 的位置有两名罪犯——Limak 确信第一座城市和第五座城市各有一名罪犯。
- 对于所有更大的距离，罪犯数量均为零。

因此，Limak 将在第一、第三和第五座城市抓捕罪犯，总共抓捕 $3$ 名罪犯。

在第二个样例中（如下图所示），BCD 告诉 Limak，距离他所在城市为 $2$ 的位置有一名罪犯。距离为 $2$ 的城市只有一座，因此 Limak 确信罪犯的位置。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c2bacc2aceaabacc98cc0dba179bc344f02aae9f.png)
